capsuleTopic.title: Israel
capsuleTopic.subtitle: Name · people · tribes · kingdoms · exile · remnant
capsuleTopic.orientation: Follow how a name given to Jacob becomes a family, a covenant people, tribes, divided kingdoms, exiles, remnants, and a later identity argued across Gospels, letters, and visions. Keep each local use of Israel, Judah, Jacob, Hebrew, and Israelite distinct.
capsuleTopic.trailPrompt: Notice who is called Israel, who speaks for the people, what binds or divides them, how their past is retold, which outsiders are present, and what each source leaves unresolved about belonging.

payload.description: Acts, letters, and Revelation revisit ancestry, remnant, covenant, identity, inclusion, warning, worship, and the twelve tribes.

nodes.title: The disciples ask about restoring the kingdom to Israel

nodes.note: Paul denies that God rejected the people, names himself an Israelite, recalls a remnant, warns Gentile branches against pride, anticipates fullness and “all Israel,” and concludes that all are shut up in disobedience for mercy.
nodes.title: Israel is discussed through remnant, branches, jealousy, and mercy

nodes.note: Paul contrasts circumcision boasting with the cross and says circumcision and uncircumcision are nothing but new creation, then speaks peace and mercy upon those walking by this rule and upon the Israel of God.

nodes.title: Jacob is renamed Israel in a night struggle

nodes.note: God appears again, repeats the new name, promises nations, kings, and land, and goes up from the place.
nodes.title: God confirms the name Israel at Bethel

nodes.note: Dinah is violated, Shechem seeks marriage, Jacob’s sons answer deceitfully, and Simeon and Levi kill the city’s males.
nodes.title: Violence brings shame upon Jacob’s household

nodes.note: Joseph reports on his brothers, receives a special garment, tells dreams, and is sent by Israel to seek the brothers’ welfare.
nodes.title: Israel sends Joseph to his brothers

nodes.note: Israel sacrifices at Beersheba, God addresses Jacob in night visions, and the household travels to Egypt.
nodes.title: Israel descends to Egypt after hearing God

nodes.note: The source names Jacob’s descendants by mothers, sons, daughters, and households and totals those entering Egypt.
nodes.title: A household is counted as the children of Israel

nodes.note: Israel claims Ephraim and Manasseh as his, crosses his hands, places the younger before the older, and blesses them.
nodes.title: Israel gives Joseph’s sons a place among his own

nodes.note: Jacob summons his sons, speaks distinct futures over them, and the narrator names them as the twelve tribes of Israel.
nodes.title: Israel speaks over the tribes before his death

payload.title: A name becomes a people

payload.description: Prophets address rebellion, election, justice, childhood, comfort, witness, false security, renewed covenant, and a cleansed name.

nodes.note: Heaven and earth hear a charge that children raised by the LORD have rebelled, worship is rejected, and washing is defined through justice for oppressed, orphan, and widow.
nodes.title: Israel is accused as rebellious children

nodes.note: A voice announces comfort, completed warfare, prepared way, enduring word, good news, divine rule, and shepherd care.
nodes.title: Comfort is spoken to a people after judgment

nodes.note: The LORD addresses Jacob and Israel by name, promises presence through waters and fire, gathers offspring, and calls the people witnesses that no other god saves.
nodes.title: Israel is called created, formed, redeemed, and witness

nodes.note: The servant speaks from a call before birth, is named Israel, laments apparently empty labor, and receives a commission to bring Jacob back and become a light to nations.
nodes.title: The servant called Israel is sent to restore Israel

nodes.note: Jeremiah stands at the Temple gate, rejects repeated trust in the building, demands justice and an end to oppression and idolatry, and points to Shiloh.
nodes.title: Temple words cannot protect an unjust people

nodes.note: The LORD promises to be God of all Israel’s families, rebuild the virgin of Israel, bring a remnant from north and ends of earth, and lead them with weeping.
nodes.title: Scattered Israel is gathered with Ephraim at the center

nodes.note: The LORD promises sowing, rebuilding, individual accountability, a new covenant unlike the exodus covenant, instruction within, universal knowing, forgiveness, and enduring national identity under cosmic order.
nodes.title: A new covenant is promised to Israel and Judah

nodes.note: Hosea’s children receive names announcing an end to Jehu’s house, no mercy, and not my people.
nodes.title: Children bear names of judgment and future reunion

nodes.note: The LORD recalls loving Israel as a child and calling the son from Egypt, yet the more Israel was called the more the people turned to Baals.
nodes.title: Israel is remembered as a loved child who turned away

nodes.note: Elders come to inquire, but the prophetic speech retells rebellion in Egypt, wilderness, and land, repeatedly saying action was taken for the divine name.
nodes.title: Ezekiel retells Israel’s rebellions and God’s name

nodes.note: Amos addresses the whole family brought from Egypt and says, “You only have I chosen,” therefore punishment follows.
nodes.title: Being known among the families brings accountability

nodes.note: Israel’s bloodshed and idolatry pollute the land, exile profanes the divine name among nations, and the LORD promises gathering, cleansing, new heart, new spirit, obedience, and restored land.
nodes.title: Israel is cleansed for the sake of a profaned name

nodes.note: Two sticks labeled for Judah and Joseph become one in the prophet’s hand, and the interpretation promises one nation, one king, cleansing, covenant of peace, sanctuary, and God’s dwelling.
nodes.title: Judah and Joseph become one stick

payload.title: Prophets accuse and promise

payload.description: Crossing, covenant, corporate guilt, repeated rescue, uneven participation, atrocity, and civil fracture test tribal solidarity.

nodes.note: The ark goes before the people, the waters stop, priests stand in the riverbed, and all Israel crosses.
nodes.title: All Israel crosses the Jordan on dry ground

nodes.note: Joshua circumcises those born in the wilderness, Israel remains at Gilgal until healing, Passover is kept, produce of the land is eaten, and manna ceases.
nodes.title: A wilderness generation is circumcised before Passover

nodes.note: Achan takes devoted property, Israel loses at Ai, and investigation narrows from people to tribe, clan, household, and person.
nodes.title: One hidden act brings defeat upon Israel

nodes.note: Joshua recounts ancestors, exodus, wilderness, land, and defeated kings, then calls for exclusive service.
nodes.title: Israel rehearses its story and chooses whom to serve

nodes.note: After Joshua’s generation dies, Israel serves other gods, faces plunderers, cries under oppression, receives judges, and turns back after each judge dies.
nodes.title: A generation forgets and a cycle begins

nodes.note: Deborah and Barak sing of willing leaders and people, the LORD’s march, tribal participation, hesitation, absence, Jael’s act, and Sisera’s waiting mother.
nodes.title: A victory song names tribes that came and tribes that stayed

nodes.note: Men surround the house, a woman is handed over, abused, and dies, and her body is divided and sent through Israel.
nodes.title: An atrocity is sent throughout Israel

nodes.note: An oath against Benjamin creates grief over a missing tribe, and Israel answers through killing at Jabesh Gilead and abducting women at Shiloh.
nodes.title: Israel tries to preserve Benjamin through further violence

payload.title: Tribes in the land

payload.description: Ark, repentance, kingship, covenant warning, tribal unity, Jerusalem, David’s house, and Temple prayer gather the people.

nodes.note: After defeat, Israel brings the ark from Shiloh expecting rescue, the camp shouts, and the Philistines fear.
nodes.title: Israel brings the ark into battle and loses it

nodes.note: Samuel calls for wholehearted return, Israel removes Baals and Ashtaroth, confesses, and asks for intercession.
nodes.title: Israel removes foreign gods and gathers at Mizpah

nodes.note: The elders cite Samuel’s sons and ask for a king to judge them, and the LORD interprets the request as rejection.
nodes.title: Israel asks for a king like the nations

nodes.note: Samuel calls down thunder during wheat harvest, the people fear and confess asking for a king, and Samuel tells them not to turn aside.
nodes.title: Thunder exposes Israel’s request, but covenant service remains open

nodes.note: The tribes name kinship, David’s earlier leadership, and the LORD’s shepherd promise, and the elders make covenant with him.
nodes.title: All Israel’s tribes anoint David king

nodes.note: David brings the ark with sacrifice, dancing, shouting, and trumpet, blesses the people, and distributes food.
nodes.title: David brings the ark into Jerusalem with celebration

nodes.note: The oracle recalls taking David from pasture, promises a name, a planted place for Israel, rest from enemies, and a dynastic house.
nodes.title: God promises Israel a place and David a house

nodes.note: At the Temple Solomon names covenant, sin, defeat, drought, famine, foreign prayer, war, captivity, forgiveness, justice, and return.
nodes.title: Solomon prays for Israel, foreigners, and future exiles

payload.title: Israel asks for a king

payload.description: Judgment, blessing, compromise, inheritance, election, love, covenant, and return are rehearsed before entry.

nodes.note: Impatience becomes accusation, fiery serpents bring death, and the people confess and ask for intercession.
nodes.title: Israel confesses after speaking against God and Moses

nodes.note: Balak builds altars and Balaam seeks a word, but the oracle asks how one can curse whom God has not cursed.
nodes.title: A hired curse becomes blessing over Israel

nodes.note: Sexual relations, sacrificial meals, and attachment to Baal bring anger and death.
nodes.title: Israel joins Baal of Peor and faces plague

nodes.note: Five women name their father, his death, lack of sons, and risk of losing his name.
nodes.title: The daughters of Zelophehad change Israel’s inheritance law

nodes.note: Moses calls Israel to hear and live, recalls Baal Peor, and says faithful practice will appear as wisdom to other peoples.
nodes.title: Israel’s life and law are displayed before nations

nodes.note: Israel is commanded to hear, love the LORD with the whole self, keep words in the heart, teach children, and mark ordinary spaces and routines.
nodes.title: Israel hears one LORD and learns daily remembrance

nodes.note: Israel is called holy and treasured, but election is explicitly denied a basis in size.
nodes.title: Israel is chosen despite being few

nodes.note: Moses binds leaders, children, foreigners, and absent generations into covenant, warns of exile, and anticipates return and heart transformation.
nodes.title: Covenant includes hidden things, exile, return, and choice

nodes.note: Moses calls heaven and earth to hear a song that names God faithful, Israel corrupt, election unearned, apostasy foreseeable, and judgment severe.
nodes.title: Moses gives Israel a song that will testify against them

payload.title: Identity before the land
